meta.title: "It's the best — everyone says so" — why your child believes confident words with no proof | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to separate bold claims from facts and ask: why is it actually "the best"? Game-based course for children aged 8–12.

hero.headline: "It's the best — everyone's already seen it!" — and your child believes it without a single "why"?
hero.subheadline: It sounds confident. But there's nothing concrete behind it. The child hears "everyone says so" — and stops asking questions.

media.alt: A child hearing confident words with no evidence behind them

pain.title: "The best" — that's not a fact, it's a claim
pain.body:
"It's the best", "everyone's already rated it", "it's top". At school, on social media, in conversations with friends. It sounds confident — but it's unclear why it's "the best". The child either believes it straight away, or gets confused: "everyone says it, so it's probably true".

This isn't being gullible or falling for advertising. It's a natural response to confident delivery: when something is said decisively and loudly, the brain tends to trust it. But "the best", "everyone", "top" — these are emotional claims with nothing behind them. No comparison, no evidence, no answer to "why".

The result — the child trusts what's said loudest, not what's actually backed up. And doesn't notice when they're being persuaded by empty words.

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
